# Incident Response SOP

## Purpose
This Standard Operating Procedure defines how the organization detects, triages,
escalates, and closes out operational incidents.

## Severity Levels and Response Times
- Severity 1 (Critical): must be acknowledged by the on-call engineer within 15 minutes
  of detection. An Incident Commander must be assigned within 30 minutes of acknowledgement.
- Severity 2 (High): must be acknowledged within 1 hour of detection.
- Severity 3 (Medium): must be acknowledged within 4 business hours.
- Severity 4 (Low): must be acknowledged within 2 business days.

## Incident Commander Responsibilities
The Incident Commander owns the incident end-to-end: coordinating responders,
communicating status to stakeholders every 30 minutes during a Severity 1 event,
and declaring when the incident is resolved.

## Escalation
If a Severity 1 incident is not acknowledged within the 15 minute window, it is
automatically escalated to the Duty Manager on-call rotation.

## Post-Incident Review
A post-incident review report is due within 5 business days after an incident is
closed. The report must include a root cause analysis and at least one corrective
action item.

## Log Retention
All incident logs, including chat transcripts and timeline entries, must be
retained for 180 days from the incident closure date.
